items.followUp: Define a molecular ion and give one example.

rubric.why: A radical is defined by its charge and its behaviour as a single unit.
rubric.description: Defines a radical as a charged atom or group of atoms behaving as a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the charge and single-unit behaviour in the definition.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a radical.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct radical, such as sulfate or ammonium.

modelAnswer: A radical is an atom or group of atoms carrying a positive or negative charge and behaving as a single unit in chemical reactions.

items.followUp: What is a diatomic molecule? Give one example.

rubric.why: The defining feature of a monoatomic molecule is that it contains one atom.
rubric.description: States that a monoatomic molecule consists of one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it consists of a single atom.

rubric.why: A noble gas provides a valid example of a monoatomic molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as helium, neon or argon.

modelAnswer: A monoatomic molecule consists of only one atom.

items.followUp: State one conclusion Rutherford drew from the alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Most alpha particles passed through the foil without deflection.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed straight through the foil.

rubric.why: A small number of alpha particles were deflected, and a very small number rebounded.
rubric.description: States another observation: some particles were deflected or a very few rebounded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct valid observation.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil without deflection.
Some alpha particles were deflected, and a very few bounced back.

items.followUp: Name one radioisotope used to treat thyroid disorders and state its use.

rubric.description: Identifies the isotopes used as tracers as radioactive isotopes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as radioactive isotopes.

rubric.why: Named examples show knowledge of isotopes used in medical tracing.
rubric.description: Names a suitable medical tracer isotope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example, such as iodine-131, phosphorus-32 or sodium-24.

modelAnswer: Radioactive isotopes are used as tracers in medicine.

items.followUp: State the periodic law proposed by Mendeleev.

rubric.why: Newlands arranged the elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
rubric.description: States the basis on which Newlands arranged the elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning increasing atomic mass.

rubric.why: The defining claim is that every eighth element had properties similar to the first.
rubric.description: States the repetition of similar properties at every eighth element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this repeating pattern.

modelAnswer: Newlands arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
He stated that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, like notes in a musical octave.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius generally decrease across a period from left to right?

rubric.why: The nuclear charge increases across a period as proton number increases.
rubric.description: States that nuclear charge increases across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the trend to increasing nuclear charge.

rubric.why: The stronger attraction between the nucleus and outer electrons makes removal of an electron more difficult.
rubric.description: Explains that increased attraction raises ionization energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the stronger nuclear attraction holds electrons more tightly.

modelAnswer: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while added electrons enter the same main shell.
The stronger attraction between the nucleus and the outer electrons makes an electron harder to remove, so ionization energy generally increases.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius increase down a group?

rubric.why: Each step down a group adds an occupied electron shell.
rubric.description: States that a new electron shell is added down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning additional shells or energy levels.

rubric.why: Greater distance and shielding reduce the effective attraction on the outer electrons.
rubric.description: Explains why the added shells make the atom larger.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking greater distance or shielding to increased atomic size.

modelAnswer: Down a group, each successive element has an additional occupied electron shell.
The outer electrons are farther from the nucleus and experience greater shielding, so atomic size increases.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and give one example of a compound containing it.

rubric.why: A chemical bond is the attractive force that keeps particles together.
rubric.description: Defines a chemical bond as a force of attraction holding atoms or ions together.

rubric.why: Ionic and covalent are two standard types of chemical bond.
rubric.description: Names any two types of chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct bond types.

modelAnswer: A chemical bond is a force of attraction that holds atoms or ions together in a substance.
Two types of chemical bond are ionic and covalent bonds.
